parsed_payload.reasoning: Let AB be the given non-parallel side and O the incircle center. Because the circle is tangent to both bases, the bases are parallel; the interior angles at A and B along the leg AB are supplementary. Since O is the incenter, AO and BO bisect those two angles. Therefore ∠OAB + ∠ABO = (∠A + ∠B)/2 = 90°. Hence in triangle AOB, ∠AOB = 180° - 90° = 90°. The given distances are OA=5 and OB=12, so AB is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and 12. Thus AB = sqrt(5^2+12^2)=sqrt(25+144)=sqrt(169)=13. The requested side length is \boxed{13}.

However, I incorrectly assumed AB=OA+OB, treating O as if it lay on side AB; O is the center of the incircle inside the trapezoid and is not generally on the leg, so these two distances are two sides of triangle AOB, not collinear segments.
Next, I will use that O lies on the angle bisectors at A and B and that the adjacent angles along a leg in a trapezoid are supplementary to show triangle AOB is right at O, then apply the Pythagorean theorem.
</reflection>
